thread:
omar_go: heads-up from the Go quickstart run: our sample app in the docker image leaked a long base64 token in the first INFO log and request IDs were missing for a handful of requests. quick repro below.

kevin_support: can you paste the tiny app + logs?

omar_go: minimal main.go: 
```
package main

import (
  "net/http"
  rws "github.com/redwood/sdk-go"
  "github.com/sirupsen/logrus"
)

func main() {
  rws.Init(rws.Config{EnableOTEL: true, Logging: rws.LoggingConfig{Level: "info", RedactPatterns: []string{"[A-Za-z0-9+/]{40,}"}}})
  http.HandleFunc("/api", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    logrus.Info("incoming payload", r.Body) // first log
    rws.LogFromRequest(r).Info("handler start")
    w.WriteHeader(200)
  })
  http.ListenAndServe(":8080", nil)
}
```
logs from docker run (sanitized):
```
2026-03-10T08:11:01Z INFO  incoming payload: eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9...
2026-03-10T08:11:01Z INFO  handler start req_id=xyz-987
```
first line: no req_id, token not redacted. second line: our structured logger shows req_id.

lucy_docs: looks like the raw log came from direct use of logrus global logger (logrus.Info) which bypasses our request-bound logger and redaction. also in Go it's common to set log output early; if we swap logger implementation after some libraries log during init, those early statements escape.

omar_go: agreed. two quibbles: (1) our Go SDK currently patches logrus by providing a hook, but it's installed during Init which happens after some library-level logs in the sample image (docker entrypoint runs `go run` quickly and some middleware logs while package init runs). (2) our redaction regex targets ASCII token chars but the token is base64 with plus and slash; my pattern included those but apparently we only apply redaction inside our logger wrapper, not the global logrus logger.

kevin_support: quick fixes?

omar_go: short-term: 1) make a synchronous console/logrus shim at the very start of Init that wraps logrus.SetFormatter/SetOutput and installs a WriteHook that runs redaction on any message passing through the global logger. 2) add rws.Env var in sample image to ensure Init runs before any app-level logging (documented in quickstart).

lucy_docs: add a short snippet to Go quickstart: call rws.Init at top of `func main()` before any package that logs gets imported, and show how to swap to rws logrus hook: `logrus.AddHook(rws.LogrusHook())`. also mention docker layering: avoid `go build` logs in ENTRYPOINT by building at image build time not runtime.

kevin_support: long-term: we should instrument the low-level stdout/stderr writer (io.Writer) in Go too, as a fallback to catch libraries that bypass logrus. also add a fuzz test that writes a variety of tokens to stdout during startup and asserts the produced logs are redacted.

infra-bot: created ticket RW-6001: "go sdk: early logrus/io.Writer shim + stdout-level redaction + quickstart doc update" assigned to omar_go, priority=P2.

omar_go: implemented a local shim: call `rws.InstallStdoutShim()` synchronously at the top of main before other work. retested in docker image: first log now contains `req_id=abc123` and payload shows `[REDACTED]`.

lucy_docs: perfect. i'll add the quickstart paragraph + minimal snippet and note the Dockerfile best-practice.

kevin_support: please also open parity ticket to check python/node for similar startup escape paths.

infra-bot: created RW-6002 for SDK parity checks across languages (assigned to kevin_support).

omar_go: thanks all. marking this as resolved for the Go quickstart. will follow up with a small CI smoke that runs the docker sample image and greps for unredacted token patterns. :white_check_mark:
